Answer: C
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates bilateral perihilar infiltrates/consolidation, and when combined with the clinical history of haemoptysis and dyspnoea, this pattern is highly characteristic of Allergic Bronchopulmonary Aspergillosis (ABPA), which typically presents with central bronchiectasis and fleeting perihilar opacities. Other options like pulmonary edema usually show cardiomegaly and Kerley B lines, while TB typically affects the upper lobes apically rather than the perihilar regions specifically.
